title: Sestini Brandbook
summary: Matilha designed Sestini’s visual identity guide: system, palette, type and applications for Brazil’s reference brand in luggage, backpacks, bags and accessories.
challenge: Sestini came to the studio with a new logo. The brief was something else: turn it into a system, with rules, palette, type and applications so institutional communication could speak with one voice, from the suitcase to the airport.
solution: We turned the mark into a method. Lockups, minimum sizes, an institutional palette and a cut of real-world applications: product, merchandising, social and media.

story.approachLead: The new logo had to become a system.
story.approach: At Matilha we started from the redrawn mark and organized what holds the communication together: brand versions, color, type and how they show up on product and in the street. Red was already Sestini. The work was giving it a setting that matches.

deliverables.title: Brand system
deliverables.body: Horizontal and vertical lockups, with and without tagline, for institutional and product contexts.

deliverables.title: Institutional palette
deliverables.body: Vermelho, Sand, Mirage and White as the core. Blue, Orange and Topaz as an extension, always at a smaller scale.

deliverables.title: Typography
deliverables.body: Unbounded for titles: geometric, wide, aligned with the symbol. Supporting text in a humanist sans for long reading.

deliverables.title: Applications
deliverables.body: From feed to billboard, luggage tag to suitcase: the brandbook proves the mark in use, not only on the board.

identity.title: The mark in every direction
identity.body: Horizontal for institutional signature, vertical for tight spaces, tagline when the line needs to travel with it. The diamond symbol, an S in two arcs, is the core that repeats from padlock to façade.

palette.title: Primary colors
palette.body: The palette puts Vermelho first, a long-standing Sestini color. Sand brings lightness to large areas. Mirage and White deliver contrast and a more contemporary tone. Secondaries widen the range, always next to the core.

type.title: Unbounded for titles
type.body: The brandbook’s display family is geometric and assertive, built for titles and high-impact pieces. On this case it is the brand’s voice. Body copy follows the studio’s reading.

inspiration.title: The palette comes from travel
inspiration.body: The secondary colors came from the tagline and from how you go: sky, land or sea. Topaz, Orange and Blue were pulled from the airplane-window photograph, then tuned to fit the Sestini palette.

graphics.title: The S becomes a graphic
graphics.body: The two arcs of the symbol become a pattern. They fill tote, suitcase, tape and ground, readable from a distance, never noise. Vermelho, Blue, Orange and Topaz carry the same drawing.

elements.title: Supporting shapes
elements.body: Shapes derived from the symbol, for more fluid compositions. They support the identity in the real world, from the horizontal band to the tape that seals the box.

applications.title: From the board into the world
applications.body: Instagram, poster, airport, accessories and product. The brandbook does not end in a PDF: it has to survive checkout, the baggage belt and the timeline.
